texts.orig: There is one more thing to be mentioned: once we have fitted our model with the data introduced in the next section, errors of w ( z i ) are correlated, i.e., the errors of w ( z i ) are dependent on each other. New parameters can be defined by transforming the covariance matrix of w ( z i ), so that errors of new parameters are decorrelated and do not entangle with each other. The new uncorrelated parameters are referred to as the principal components [10, 23], and they are directly related to their own locations (unlike the correlated case). So errors of the uncorrelated parameters are more interpretable and meaningful. For more discussions and implications of the uncorrelated parameters, we refer to the references [11, 14, 24].
